unlisted_practices: Have subject matter experts, ideally specialist mental health clinicians, review the mental status examination data corpus to guide its conceptual organization before using it for research.
Operationally define the psychopathological constructs that MSE data will be mapped to by prioritizing consensus sources such as DSM-5 or ICD-11, and use the MCCB for cognitive symptoms.
Explicitly distinguish formal psychopathological constructs, their descriptions in reference sources, and the MSE findings indicative of them when organizing MSE data.
Distinguish direct, synonymous, and downstream manifestation relationships between MSE findings and psychopathological constructs, recognizing that each level requires more clinical interpretation.
Pre-specify the conceptual scheme for mapping MSE findings and formally assess its interrater reliability using standard methods.

Critically appraise the provenance of MSE data, including clinical setting, clinician background, specialty, acuity, and time constraints, and temper confidence in findings and generalizability accordingly.
Interpret longitudinal changes in documented MSE findings with caution, as they may reflect changes in documentation practices rather than genuine changes in psychopathology.

Evaluate whether NLP technologies guided by a ground-truth corpus of conceptually organized MSE data can extract and distinguish direct from indirect descriptions of psychopathology with strong classification performance.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual commentary/perspective article examining the methodological and clinical principles for using NLP and LLMs to extract mental status examination (MSE) data from EHRs for psychiatric research.
